pool.text: The city was founded as a nomadic Buddhist monastic centre.
The Vajradhara statue was made by Zanabazar himself.
The Treaty of Kyakhta regulated Qing-Russian trade.
The city was permanently settled at its modern location.
The 5th Bogd Jebtsundamba moved his residence to Gandan Hill.
The camp part that moved to Tolgoit was brought back.
The Choijin Lama Monastery was turned into a museum.
The Gandan Monastery was reopened.
The Mongolian State Grand National Orchestra was established.
Chingeltei District was established as part of the public library system organization.
The Trans-Mongolian Railway connecting the cities was completed.
Bayanzurkh District was established as part of the public library system organization.
Its original Artificial Lake Castle was built.
The Children's Central Library was established to serve young readers in the city.
The Ulaanbaatar government created a centralized system known as the Metropolitan Library System.
Large demonstrations led to Mongolia's transition to democracy.
The major book fair was held first, attracting numerous book authors and publishing houses.
Ulaanbaatar was the scene of riots after disputed elections.
The National Garden Park opened in the southeastern outskirts.
Ulaanbaatar hosted the 7th Ministerial Conference.
